name: EVOSST
title: Evaluation and Valorization of Social Services for a Sustainable Transition
institution: National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest
funding: Horizon Europe · Research and Innovation Action
summary: Predictive modelling and data analysis to understand the long-term impact of social services.
description: EVOSST develops life-course assessment models for healthcare, childcare, long-term care, education and social inclusion. The consortium combines well-being measures and digital technologies to support more effective, evidence-informed social policies.
contributions: Collecting and processing datasets relevant to social-service impact assessment.
Developing predictive models for the long-term effects of services in healthcare, education and social inclusion.
Visualising results to support interpretation and their use in public-policy development.
details: Coordinator: University of Western Macedonia, Greece.
Call: HORIZON-CL2-2024-TRANSFORMATIONS-01-04.

name: Renewable district heating
title: Feasibility study for the integration of solar and wind energy into district heating systems using advanced heat storage solutions
funding: EEA Grants 2014–2021 and Norway Grants 2014–2021 · Bilateral Cooperation for the Green Transition
summary: Solar and wind integration with advanced heat storage for ELCEN’s district-heating system.
description: The feasibility study assessed how solar and wind energy could be integrated into ELCEN’s district-heating system in Bucharest, supported by advanced heat storage. AUDIT IT&C worked with Norsk Energi and ELECTROCENTRALE BUCUREȘTI (ELCEN) to evaluate technical options, economic viability and future investment opportunities. The work combined technical assessments, cost–benefit analysis and recommendations for reducing fossil-fuel dependence and improving thermal-system efficiency.
contributions: Directed research and project-management activities.
Analysed Best Available Technology (BAT) for integrating renewable sources into thermal-energy production.
Assessed optimal heat-storage solutions for the proposed district-heating integration.
details: Project promoter: AUDIT IT&C SRL, Romania.
Norwegian partner: Norsk Energi, contributing expertise in advanced heat storage.
Main beneficiary: ELECTROCENTRALE BUCUREȘTI SA (ELCEN), Romania.
Activities included the feasibility study, training and knowledge exchange between Romanian and Norwegian partners, and dissemination events.
Funding countries: Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.

name: TwinEU
title: Digital Twin for Europe
institution: National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest
summary: A federated digital twin of Europe’s electricity system for resilient operation, forecasting and coordinated planning.
description: TwinEU is developing a pan-European electricity-system digital twin by connecting local and regional twins through interoperable data and model exchanges. It combines physical modelling, artificial intelligence and high-performance computing to support grid operation, market coordination and renewable-energy integration. The architecture links adaptive digital twins, a trusted data-sharing layer and a service workbench for reusable applications and computing resources.
contributions: Contributed to the project’s research activities as a senior researcher.
details: Coordinator: Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, Germany.
Eight demonstrators across eleven countries address grid resilience, monitoring and operation, forecasting and market decisions, and coordinated network planning.
The wider collaboration spans fifteen European countries and includes POLITEHNICA Bucharest.
Interoperability is supported by standard interfaces, open APIs and connections to energy data spaces.
Funding topic: HORIZON-CL5-2023-D3-01-10.

name: SMARTELTER
title: Green Mobile Services for Smart City Energy Systems
funding: Competitiveness Operational Programme (POC) · Action 1.2.1 · Innovative Technological Project
summary: Mobile battery storage, solar charging and AI-based management for urban electricity and heating services.
description: SMARTELTER focused on a mobile energy-service system combining lithium-ion battery platforms, photovoltaic generation, electric-vehicle charging and hot-water production. An artificial-intelligence management platform was designed to coordinate operating parameters, locations and routes while optimising electricity generation and use. The project targeted a prototype integrating hardware, software and energy management, alongside a new production unit.
contributions: Directed the project's research and management activities.
Led work within the Innovative Technological Project funding framework.
details: Four planned mobile lithium-ion battery platforms: 50, 200, 300 and 500 kWh.
Energy services: a 0.1 MW electric water-heating system and 22 kW and 50 kW electric-vehicle chargers.
Solar charging: a container with deployable photovoltaic panels rated at 40 kW.
Prototype work covered design, construction, testing, an operating manual and an AI module.
Funding: European Regional Development Fund through the Competitiveness Operational Programme 2014–2020; call POC/1033/1/3.

name: Resilient nanogrids
title: Resilient and Self-Recovering Nano Electric Networks
funding: National Plan PN III (2013–2020) · Horizon 2020 Participation Award
summary: National support for participation in European research on resilient, self-recovering electrical nanogrids.
description: A competitively awarded national project supporting Horizon 2020 participation and research on resilient electrical nanogrids. This award is a separate project-director appointment from the senior-researcher role in ELECTRON.
contributions: Directed research activities and project management.
Managed the competitively awarded national participation-support project.
details: Internal project code: 220214299.
Submission contract: 101021936 / 01.10.2021.
The budget shown belongs to this national award, not the full ELECTRON consortium.

name: ELECTRON
title: rEsilient and seLf-healed EleCTRical pOwer Nanogrid
institution: National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest
summary: Cybersecurity, resilience and recovery for electrical power and energy systems.
description: ELECTRON developed an integrated approach to protecting electrical power and energy systems against cyber, privacy and data attacks. Its four pillars cover risk assessment and certification, anomaly detection and prevention, failure mitigation and energy restoration, and AR/VR-based personnel training.
contributions: Contributed as a senior researcher within the POLITEHNICA Bucharest team.
details: Coordinator: NETCOMPANY SA, Belgium.
Topic: SU-DS04-2018-2020 — cybersecurity in electrical power and energy systems.

name: STOCMAN
title: Intelligent Management System for Improving the Efficiency of Battery Storage Systems based on Pb-acid and Li-Ion Batteries
funding: POC · Priority Axis 1 · Action 1.2.1 · Innovation of Products and Services in an Innovative Start-Up
summary: Fuzzy-logic control and battery balancing for more efficient lead-acid and lithium-ion energy storage.
description: STOCMAN developed an intelligent battery-management approach for lead-acid and lithium-ion energy-storage systems. Its proposed equipment used fuzzy logic to optimise charging and discharging, balance the voltages of component batteries without dissipating balancing energy, shorten charging time and improve battery life and storage efficiency. The work supported new products and services based on intelligent energy-storage technology.
contributions: Directed the project's research activities.
Managed the research and development project within the POC funding framework.
details: Project code: SMIS 115939.
Host company: ADEMA EQUIP SRL.
Funding: Competitiveness Operational Programme 2014–2020; Priority Axis 1, Action 1.2.1.
Implementation period: 15 months.
Technical focus: fuzzy-logic charge/discharge control, battery-voltage balancing and improved energy-storage efficiency.

name: LargCoat
title: Innovative Technologies for Physical Vapor Deposition Based on Thin, Multifunctional, Nanostructured Layers for Large Components
summary: Research participation in large-component physical-vapour-deposition technologies.
description: The project investigated physical vapour deposition technologies using thin, multifunctional, nanostructured layers for large components.
contributions: Performed research activities as a member of the Politehnica University of Bucharest team.
details: Project code: 122543.

name: ProSSSy
title: Autonomous Polymorphic Robotic Platforms for Smart City Services
funding: European Regional Development Fund · Competitiveness Operational Programme 2014–2020
summary: Modular autonomous robots for healthcare assistance, guidance and monitoring in smart cities.
description: ProSSSy investigated autonomous, adaptable robotic platforms for services in smart cities. A common mobile base could carry different application modules, allowing the same robotic architecture to support health-check kiosks, visitor guidance, advertising and perimeter monitoring. Its layered design combined navigation and movement with interchangeable service applications for use in buildings and urban spaces.
contributions: Contributed to the project’s research activities as a senior researcher.
details: Project company: LIGHTNING NET SRL, Romania.
Research partner: Politehnica University of Bucharest.
Technical scope: autonomous or assisted movement, modular applications, electronics, mechanics, IT and remote monitoring.
Application areas included healthcare assistance, security, tourism and education.
Project implementation: 36 months.

name: FARCROSS
title: FAcilitating Regional CROSS-border Electricity Transmission through Innovation
summary: Improving cross-border electricity flows, grid observability and regional coordination.
description: FARCROSS brought together energy-system stakeholders to demonstrate hardware and software that increase the use of transmission assets and support regional cooperation. Its scope includes dynamic line rating, wide-area protection, renewable-generation forecasting, reserve optimisation and regulatory barriers to cross-border flows.
contributions: Performed research activities as a research assistant at Politehnica University of Bucharest.
details: Topic: LC-SC3-ES-2-2019 — regional cross-border cooperation in transmission grids.
The funding amounts represent the entire consortium.

name: FLEXITRANSTORE
title: An Integrated Platform for Increased Flexibility in Smart Transmission Grids with Storage Entities and Large Penetration of Renewable Energy Sources
summary: Storage, demand response and flexibility markets for renewable-rich transmission networks.
description: FLEXITRANSTORE developed a flexible energy-grid platform combining storage, demand response, control improvements and electricity-market mechanisms. Eight demonstrations across six countries addressed renewable integration, cross-border electricity exchange and more effective use of existing grid infrastructure.
contributions: Contributed research as a member of the Politehnica University of Bucharest team.
details: Coordinator: European Dynamics Belgium.
Demonstration countries: Greece, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Slovenia, Belgium and Spain.
The consortium duration and budget are separate from the individual appointment.

name: INTERRFACE
title: TSO-DSO-Consumer INTERFACE aRchitecture to provide innovative grid services for an efficient power system
summary: Coordinating transmission operators, distribution operators and consumers through interoperable grid services.
description: INTERRFACE developed an Interoperable pan-European Grid Services Architecture (IEGSA) connecting transmission system operators (TSOs), distribution system operators (DSOs) and consumers. The project addressed coordinated procurement of balancing, congestion-management and ancillary services, enabling distributed renewable generation, storage and demand response to participate more effectively in electricity markets.
details: Coordinator: European Dynamics Luxembourg SA, Luxembourg.
Digital tools combined big-data management and blockchain technologies to support consumer participation and the use of distributed energy resources.
Politehnica University of Bucharest participated in the consortium, with an EU contribution of €450,000.
The duration and total funding shown describe the consortium project.

name: Electromagnetic launcher
title: Electromagnetic Launcher for Extinguishing Violent Fires in Drilling Operations and Launching Drones for Investigations or Interventions
summary: Research on electromagnetic launch systems for emergency intervention and investigation.
description: A research assignment concerning electromagnetic launching for intervention in drilling-operation fires and the deployment of investigation or intervention drones.
contributions: Contributed to the project as a research assistant at Politehnica University of Bucharest.
details: Project director: Sorin Dan Grigorescu.

name: Electrical-network monitoring
title: Integrated Monitoring and Control System for Real-Time Complete Estimation of the Functional State of Electrical Network Assemblies
summary: Real-time monitoring, control and functional-state estimation of electrical network assemblies.
description: An integrated-system research assignment focused on monitoring and control for the real-time estimation of the operating state of electrical-network assemblies.
contributions: Contributed to the project as a research assistant at Politehnica University of Bucharest.
details: Project director: Victor Ursianu.

name: 3D dental e-learning
title: Virtual E-Learning Platform Based on 3D Applications for Use in Dental Prosthetics
summary: A virtual learning platform using three-dimensional applications in dental prosthetics.
description: A research assignment on a virtual e-learning platform for dental prosthetics, using three-dimensional applications to support training.
contributions: Contributed to the project as a research assistant at Politehnica University of Bucharest.
details: Project director: Simona Andreea Sandu.
